page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-60 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the t2d family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The configuration features 60 dedicated physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, providing a total of 60 vCPUs. It includes 240.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the t2d-standard-60 demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core tests. It also achieves strong results in multi-threaded workloads, including bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core execution, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory performance is strong for cached small-block reads, though uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the average range. Cryptographic and database operations, such as Redis SET commands, also perform in the top 25%.

While the instance excels at multi-threaded processing and prompt processing for small to medium language models, it exhibits limitations in large-scale AI generation. Specifically, LLM text generation using a large 70B model falls into the bottom 25% of benchmarks, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. Given its high physical core count and balanced memory allocation, the t2d-standard-60 is suited for multi-threaded compilation, database operations, web serving, and general-purpose enterprise workloads that require dedicated CPU resources without hyperthreading overhead.
